 Lee Jae Wook’s Dead-End Job Is Now Streaming on Netflix
 Sweety High Staff 
 Oct 30, 2026
 Netflix has released all eight episodes of the K-drama Dead-End Job today, Oct. 30, with Lee Jae Wook leading the cast.
 The fantasy-horror series follows a man buried in debt who takes a part-time job that pays far too well, which makes it a perfect watch for Halloween weekend.
 ( Dead-End Job via Netflix)
 Release date: Oct. 30
 Where to watch: Netflix (all eight episodes)
 Cast: Lee Jae Wook, Go Min Si, Kim Min Ha and Lee Hee Joon
 Director: Kim Da Min
 Genre: Mystery, fantasy and horror
 ‘When Can You Watch Dead-End Job on Netflix?’
 The series is streaming now, and Netflix dropped the full season at once.
 That means you can binge all eight episodes over the weekend, which is exactly how the premiere date was timed.
 ‘What Is Dead-End Job About?’
 Hyeok Jun, played by Lee Jae Wook, is drowning in debt when he spots a flyer for a part-time gig at the Spider Staffing Agency.
 Netflix’s synopsis says the job pays 50 times the usual hourly wage, and it comes with one rule: never reveal what happens on the job.
 He is sent to what looks like an ordinary convenience store, but every shift quickly turns into a fight for survival.
 The trailer shows a very tired Hyeok Jun sitting across from the cheerful boss of the agency, who insists there is no better job out there.
 ‘Who Is in the Cast?’
 Lee Jae Wook is best known to K-drama fans for Alchemy of Souls and Dear Hongrang .
 Go Min Si plays Yeon Ju, an investigator who digs into the strange events at the agency, and she previously starred in Sweet Home and The Frog .
 Kim Min Ha plays Hyeok Jun’s younger sister, Ji Yoon, who lives by the idea that poverty is scarier than ghosts.
 Lee Hee Joon plays Mr. S, the unsettling boss of the agency, and Choi Hyun Wook and Yoon Kyung Ho also appear.
Also read about: The Biggest Horror Movies and Shows Arriving This October 
 ‘Who Is Behind the Series?’
 Kim Da Min directs and previously wrote the Netflix series A Killer Paradox .
 Han Jun Hee, the creator of Weak Hero Class 1 and a writer and director on D.P. , serves as executive producer and leads the overall creative development.
 The series was filmed from April to October 2025 and was originally known as Perfect Job .
 With a mix of dark comedy, supernatural scares and a very relatable fear of bad jobs, it is a good pick if you want something spooky that isn’t a traditional horror movie.
